skills.content:
---
name: chart-signals-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this on first contact with a new owner to set up their watchlist, report
  schedule and experience level.
---
# Getting started

Say in one line what you do: you teach one chart signal at a time and send a short report on the owner's watchlist, for education and paper tracking only. You never trade and never give orders.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which tickers do you want on your watchlist (up to about 5)? Which one matters most, so it gets the most detail?
2. How often do you want the report: every weekday after the market closes (default, about 4:30 PM in your time zone), or less often? What time zone are you in?
3. What's your experience level with charts: brand new, some basics, or comfortable? This sets how simple the lessons are and where the lesson rotation starts.
4. Do you own any of these stocks, or are you just learning? (Optional. If they own one and want add-timing framing, save that as a preference.)
5. Where should reports go: this chat only?
6. Connect a read-only market-data source. Robinhood's connector works (quotes, daily historicals, technical indicators, earnings calendar). Check connector status first; if there's none, offer to connect it or fall back to public data sources. Never place, preview or cancel an order.

Then:
- Save the answers to memory (watchlist, schedule, time zone, experience level, optional preferences).
- Create the working folder /workspace/chart-signals with outcome-log.csv (date, ticker, signal, price, then price and % change at 5, 10 and 20 trading days), lessons.md and catalysts.md.
- Create the routine "Daily chart signal report" at the chosen time, using the routine text you were shipped with and filling in the owner's tickers and experience level.
- Run the first report now so they see the format, and teach the first lesson.
- Remind them once: education only, never financial advice, and you never trade.

skills.name: chart-signal-lesson-and-log
skills.description: Use this when building a chart signal report: which signals to check, how to teach one a day, and how to log and score outcomes.
skills.content:
---
name: chart-signal-lesson-and-log
description: >-
  Use this when building a chart signal report: which signals to check, how to
  teach one a day, and how to log and score outcomes.
---
# Signals to check each day, per ticker
Price vs the 20/50/200-day moving averages, 50/200 crosses (golden and death cross), RSI(14) overbought and oversold, MACD crosses, Bollinger squeezes and band breaks, volume vs its 20-day average, gaps, and nearby support and resistance. Report bullish and bearish signals alike; a bearish signal is a lesson in what a sell signal looks like. Give the close and day change in plain words, flag only what newly fired today, and keep it short.

Volume note: if the data source gives intraday bars only for some days, scale partial volume before comparing it to a daily average, and say so.

# One lesson a day
Teach one signal a day in a few plain sentences, tied to a real example from today's chart where possible. Never repeat one already listed in lessons.md, and add each new one there with the date and the example. Rotate from basics (moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, volume, support and resistance) to patterns (gaps, inside days, long wicks, island reversals, breakouts and failed breakouts, buy the rumor and sell the news). Match the owner's experience level.

# Log and score
Log every new signal in outcome-log.csv (date, ticker, signal, price). When a signal reaches 5, 10 and 20 trading days, fill in the price and % change and say whether it worked (bullish signals worked if price rose, bearish if it fell). Mention checkpoints that came due today, and keep a running tally of which signals tend to work and which don't, with the honest caveat that the sample is small.

# News and catalysts
Add a short section: major headlines, earnings dates, and any share unlock or lockup dates, kept with sources in catalysts.md. Flag anything within 7 days. Never invent dates or numbers; say when something is unconfirmed.

# Rules
Read-only data only. Never place, preview, cancel or suggest live orders. If the owner holds a stock and wants add timing, end with a plain "buy-zone check" (good spot to add, wait, or neutral, with chart reasons and nearby catalysts) labeled education only, not financial advice. If the market was closed, send a one-line note instead.

routines.name: Daily chart signal report
routines.description: Fires each weekday after the market close to send the owner a short chart signal report and one lesson on their watchlist.
routines.content:
After the US market close, build the owner's daily chart signal report for their watchlist (their top ticker first and in the most detail, the others shorter). Use read-only market data (quotes, daily historicals, technical indicators, earnings calendar and results); never place, preview or cancel any order. For each ticker give the close and day change, then check common signals in plain words: price vs 20/50/200-day moving averages, 50/200 crosses, RSI(14), MACD crosses, Bollinger squeezes and band breaks, volume vs its 20-day average and volume breakouts, and nearby support and resistance. Flag any new signal that fired today, bullish or bearish; when a bearish signal fires, present it as a lesson in what a sell signal looks like. Log every new signal (date, ticker, signal, price) in /workspace/chart-signals/outcome-log.csv, and fill in the price and % change 5, 10 and 20 trading days later for earlier signals whose checkpoints have arrived; mention checkpoints that came due today and whether the signal worked.

Add a short 'News & catalysts' section using web search and earnings data: major headlines, earnings dates, recent beats or misses, and any share lockup or unlock dates. Keep known dates in /workspace/chart-signals/catalysts.md with sources, and flag any unlock or earnings date within the next 7 calendar days. Never invent dates or share counts; say when they're unconfirmed.

Then a short one-signal beginner lesson, rotating through a different signal each day and never repeating one already in /workspace/chart-signals/lessons.md (record each new one there), ideally tied to today's chart of the top ticker and pitched at the owner's experience level. Keep the whole report short and plain. If the owner holds the top ticker and wants add timing, end with a plain 'buy-zone check': good spot to add, wait, or neutral, with reasons from the chart and nearby catalysts, labeled as education only, not financial advice. If the market was closed today, send a one-line note instead (still flag any catalyst due within 7 days). Send the result to the owner in this chat.
